read.thesis: Gildan's Q4 is HanesBrands-inflated; the real signal is a deliberate inventory cut and plant closures, with 2026 Q1 sales guided to ~$1.15B and adjusted margin to 12.9%. Supply discipline is improving, but guidance is soft in the near term.

capex.quote: with the required capital expenditure expected to remain within our capex guidance

triggers.label: Two HanesBrands textile plants closed early 2026
triggers.quote: the Company is proceeding with the closure of HanesBrands' two textile manufacturing facilities in early 2026

triggers.label: Synergy target raised to $250M
triggers.quote: approximately $250 million (versus $200 million originally expected) of annual run-rate cost synergies

triggers.label: Temporary channel inventory reduction
triggers.quote: we are proactively undertaking a temporary reduction of inventory across our combined customer channels

triggers.label: Q1 2026 sales ~$1.15B, margin 12.9%
triggers.quote: For the first quarter of 2026, net sales from continuing operations are expected to be approximately $1.15 billion

guidance.quote: Full year adjusted operating margin of approximately 20%;
Adjusted diluted EPS in the range of $4.20 to $4.40
Free cash flow to be above $850 million.
Capex to come in at approximately 3% of net sales;
net sales from continuing operations are expected to be approximately $1.15 billion
Adjusted operating margin is expected to be approximately 12.9%
approximately $250 million (versus $200 million originally expected) of annual run-rate cost synergies

guidance.value: 3-5% CAGR sales; low-20% adj EPS growth
guidance.quote: Company maintains its three-year objectives for the 2026–2028 period

red_flags.label: Net debt leverage 3.0x vs 1.5-2.5x target
red_flags.quote: We ended the year with net debt of $4,417 million and a leverage ratio of 3.0 times
